Must (e_i) be equivalent to the unit vector basis of c_0 or l_1? If not, characterize all such bases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(e_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ be a normalized monotone subsymmetric basis of a Banach space $X$ (i.e., $(e_i)$ is a Schauder basis with basis constant $1$ that is equivalent, with the same constants, to all of its subsequences). Two basic sequences $(u_i)_{i=1}^n$ and $(v_i)_{i=1}^n$ are called $C$-equivalent if for every choice of scalars $(a_i)_{i=1}^n$,
$$ C^{-1} \Bigl\| \sum_{i=1}^n a_i u_i \Bigr\| \le \Bigl\| \sum_{i=1}^n a_i v_i \Bigr\| \le C \Bigl\| \sum_{i=1}^n a_i u_i \Bigr\|. $$

Assume that $(e_i)$ has the following property: for each constant $C \ge 1$ there exists a constant $D \ge 1$ such that every normalized weakly null sequence $(x_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ in any Banach space $Y$ admits a subsequence $(y_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ with the following stabilization property — whenever $i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_n$ are indices such that $(y_{i_j})_{j=1}^n$ is $C$-equivalent to $(e_i)_{i=1}^n$, one has
$$ \Bigl\| \sum_{j=1}^n a_{i_j} y_{i_j} \Bigr\| \le D \,\Bigl\| \sum_{j=1}^\infty a_j y_j \Bigr\| $$
for every scalar sequence $(a_j)_{j=1}^\infty$ (whenever the right-hand side is finite).

Question. Must $(e_i)$ be equivalent to the unit vector basis of $c_0$ or of $\ell_1$? If not, give a characterization of all normalized monotone subsymmetric bases $(e_i)$ satisfying the above property.

Related work on weakly null sequences, spreading models, and subsymmetric basic sequences exists, but no source clearly settles or partially settles this specific problem.
